page: Microsoft Azure E48s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware allocation provides 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores across two threads per core, alongside a large 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, sustaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor includes hardware acceleration extensions such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and Intel SHA extensions. The instance includes no integrated local storage and contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel computing and memory throughput capabilities. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,316.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 60,432.72, both placing in the top 25%. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reached 190.66 GB/sec, supporting fast streaming across large working sets. In-memory workloads perform efficiently, demonstrated by 63.01 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware vector extensions also translate into high performance for compute-intensive tasks, highlighted by an image processing score of 19,241.0 in Geekbench, placing it in the top 10%.

In terms of tradeoffs, single-thread performance metrics—such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1,940.0 and stress-ng single-core output of 1,766.18—remain within the middle 50% baseline. PassMark memory testing returned lower comparative scores (1,645.83). Additionally, because this instance configuration does not include local ephemeral disks, all persistent and scratch storage requirements depend entirely on remote network-attached disks.

The 1:8 core-to-memory configuration delivers high resource density for memory-bound deployments. Microsoft Azure E48s_v6 is well suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large Redis caches, memory-intensive data analytics, and CPU-based machine learning inference pipelines leveraging AMX matrix acceleration.
